---
title: "School finances before closure"
subtitle: "What happened to the pupil numbers and finances of state schools in the years before they closed, and what that says about early warning for others."
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
source(here::here("R", "site_helpers.R"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(data.table); library(leaflet) })
F <- readRDS(here::here("data", "finance_closures.rds"))
DEM <- readRDS(here::here("data", "demographics.rds"))
PRO <- F$profile; BEN <- F$benchmark; TE <- F$test; EFF <- F$effects
pm <- function(st, v, kk, col = "median") PRO[stage == st & measure == v & k == kk][[col]]
bm <- function(st, v) BEN[stage == st & measure == v, median]
nc <- function(st) F$n_closers[stage == st, schools]
def_open <- F$deficit_all[, .(d = mean(deficit)), by = stage]
dk <- function(st, kk) F$deficit_k[stage == st & k == kk, deficit]
sr <- F$sign_rates
sr_at <- function(st, n) sr[stage == st & n_signs == n, rate]
cap <- function(x) paste0(toupper(substr(x, 1, 1)), substring(x, 2))
K_LAB <- c(`-6` = "6 years\nbefore", `-5` = "5", `-4` = "4", `-3` = "3", `-2` = "2", `-1` = "1 year\nbefore", `0` = "Last\nyear")
fin_years <- range(F$years)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## In short

- **Rolls fall first, and furthest.** Of the `r nc("Primary")` state primary
  schools that closed or merged from 2017/18 on, the typical one had lost
  `r pts(abs(pm("Primary", "pupils_chg3", -4)), 0)`% of its pupils over three
  years four years before it closed, and `r pts(abs(pm("Primary", "pupils_chg3", -1)), 0)`%
  by the year before, when it was `r pts(pm("Primary", "util", -1), 0)`% full
  against `r pts(bm("Primary", "util"), 0)`% for schools that stayed open.
- **The money follows.** Their reserves and in-year balances were close to
  other schools' six years out and weakened as the end neared: in the year
  before closing, `r pts(dk("Primary", -1), 0)`% were in deficit, against
  about `r pts(def_open[stage == "Primary", d], 0)`% of open primary schools in
  a typical year. Income per pupil rose, because a shrinking school keeps its
  fixed costs and lump sums.
- **There is early warning in schools' own returns.** A simple model of
  pupils, capacity and finances, trained on closures up to 2020/21, picked
  out the schools that closed later: the riskiest 5% of returns included
  `r round(100 * TE$early$top5[["caught"]] / TE$early$top5[["closures"]])`% of
  the returns from schools that closed two or three years on. Rolls carry most of the
  warning; finances add to it.
- **No open school is named here.** The page counts schools showing the
  warning signs by authority. A published list could itself push a school
  towards closure, as parents and staff read it.
:::

Every state mainstream school that closed with no successor, or merged
into another, from 2017/18 to 2025/26 (from
[Pupil numbers and school places](demographics.qmd#sec-demog-data)) is
followed back through its finance returns: maintained schools' Consistent
Financial Reporting (CFR) from `r fin_years[1]` and academies' accounts
returns (AAR) from 2016-17, to `r fin_years[2]`. A school that became an
academy before it closed is followed through both. Each school's figures are
set against all the state schools of its stage still open that year. That is
`r nc("Primary")` primary and `r nc("Secondary")` secondary schools; most of
what follows is about primary schools, where nearly all closures are.

## The years before closure {#sec-before}

```{r}
#| label: fig-before
#| fig-cap: "Primary schools that closed or merged from 2017/18: the median school (line) and the middle half (band) in each year before closure, against the median open primary school (dashed). Pupils are full-time equivalents from the finance returns; capacity is GIAS's."
#| fig-height: 7
v6 <- c("pupils", "pupils_chg3", "util", "reserve_pct", "in_year_pct", "income_pp")
d <- PRO[stage == "Primary" & measure %in% v6][, lab := factor(F$measures[measure], F$measures[v6])]
b <- BEN[stage == "Primary" & measure %in% v6][, lab := factor(F$measures[measure], F$measures[v6])]
ggplot(d, aes(k, median)) + geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q1, ymax = q3), fill = LPURPLE, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(data = b, aes(yintercept = median), linetype = "dashed", colour = GREY) +
  geom_line(colour = DPURPLE, linewidth = 1.1) + geom_point(colour = DPURPLE, size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~lab, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = -6:0, labels = K_LAB) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) + theme_note(11)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-percentile
#| fig-cap: "The same schools as percentiles among all open primary schools that year (50 = the middle). Below 50: smaller, emptier, falling faster, or with less in reserve than most schools."
#| fig-height: 4.4
pp <- PRO[stage == "Primary" & measure %in% v6 & !is.na(p_median)][, lab := factor(F$measures[measure], F$measures[v6])]
ggplot(pp, aes(k, p_median, colour = lab)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 50, colour = GREY) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) + geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(DPURPLE, BPURPLE, MPURPLE, BLUE, "#5aae61", GREY)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = -6:-1, labels = K_LAB[1:6]) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Median percentile", colour = NULL) + theme_note(11) + guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

The order matters. Six years before closure the schools that went on to
close were already smaller than most (median percentile
`r pts(pm("Primary", "pupils", -6, "p_median"), 0)`) and had begun to lose
pupils; their finances were near the middle. Rolls kept falling and capacity
emptying, year on year; reserves and in-year balances slipped only in the
last two or three years. A school's finances, in other words, mostly record
what its rolls have already done: by the time the deficit shows, the
pupils have gone.

```{r}
#| label: fig-deficit
#| fig-cap: "Share of closing primary and secondary schools with a negative revenue reserve, in each year before closure, against the share of open schools in an average year (dashed)."
#| fig-height: 3.8
dd <- F$deficit_k[k <= 0]
ggplot(dd, aes(k, deficit)) + geom_col(fill = MPURPLE, width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(data = def_open, aes(yintercept = d), linetype = "dashed", colour = GREY) +
  facet_wrap(~stage) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = -6:0, labels = K_LAB) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "% in deficit") + theme_note(11)
```

Secondary closures are few (`r nc("Secondary")` since 2017/18) and more varied,
but show the same order: rolls first, then money.

## Which signals warn, and how early {#sec-model}

A logistic regression asks, for every school-year from 2017-18 to 2023-24,
whether the school closed within the next two years, given that year's
return. Each signal's effect is shown per standard deviation (or yes against
no), holding the others fixed.

```{r}
#| label: fig-effects
#| fig-cap: "Odds of closing within two years, per standard deviation of each signal (or yes against no), with 95% intervals. Below 1, less likely to close; solid points are clear of 1."
#| fig-height: 4.6
e <- EFF[, .(label = factor(label, rev(label)), or, lo, hi, clear = lo > 1 | hi < 1, per)]
ggplot(e, aes(or, label)) + geom_vline(xintercept = 1, colour = GREY) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), colour = DPURPLE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = clear), colour = DPURPLE, size = 2.6, fill = "white", stroke = 1) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 19, `FALSE` = 21), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2)) + labs(x = "Odds ratio (log scale)", y = NULL) + theme_note(11)
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## The model behind this chart

$$\text{logit}\,\Pr(\text{closes within two years})_{st} = \beta_0 + \sum_j \beta_j x_{jst}$$

for school *s* in year *t*, with the signals $x_j$ as in the chart (a school
three years old or more, with at least 10 pupils and a return with income).
Percentages are capped (change in pupils at ±50, capacity 20 to 150, reserve
±40, in-year balance ±20) so that a few odd returns cannot steer it.

```r
glm(y ~ log_pupils + chg3 + util_c + res + iy + ipp + area_primary_chg + academy + secondary,
    family = binomial, data = mm)   # `r format(F$model$n, big.mark = ",")` school-years, `r F$model$events` closing within two years
```

The full method (how the sample is built, the coefficients, the tests,
calibration and limits) is in [the methodology](method.qmd#sec-finance-method).
:::

The strongest single sign is a falling roll: each standard deviation more of
fall over three years more than doubles the odds. An emptier school, a
smaller reserve, an in-year deficit, a small school and an area whose primary
population is falling all add. Academies are much less likely to close than
maintained schools with the same figures. That is partly how the system
works rather than how the schools are doing: a struggling academy is more
often moved to another trust than closed. Income per pupil goes the other
way because, size for size, a school with more per pupil is one that has
lost pupils faster than its funding.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-test
#| tbl-cap: "How well the model picks out closures it was not trained on: fitted on 2017-18 to 2020-21, tested on 2021-22 to 2023-24. AUC is the chance a closing school is ranked above an open one (0.5 is guessing)."
tt <- data.table(
  Test = c("Closes within two years", "Closes two or three years on (early)"),
  AUC = sprintf("%.2f", c(TE$auc, TE$early$auc)),
  `Closing in test years` = c(TE$top2[["closures"]], TE$early$top2[["closures"]]),
  `Caught in riskiest 2%` = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", c(TE$top2[["caught"]], TE$early$top2[["caught"]]),
                                     100 * c(TE$top2[["caught"]] / TE$top2[["closures"]], TE$early$top2[["caught"]] / TE$early$top2[["closures"]])),
  `Caught in riskiest 5%` = sprintf("%d (%.0f%%)", c(TE$top5[["caught"]], TE$early$top5[["caught"]]),
                                     100 * c(TE$top5[["caught"]] / TE$top5[["closures"]], TE$early$top5[["caught"]] / TE$early$top5[["closures"]])))
kt(tt, align = "lrrrr")
```

Pupil numbers and capacity alone give an AUC of `r sprintf("%.2f", TE$parts[["rolls"]])`
on the test years; the finance measures alone
`r sprintf("%.2f", TE$parts[["finance"]])`; maintained or academy alone
`r sprintf("%.2f", TE$parts[["governance"]])`. Both kinds of signal carry
warning, and together they do better than either. Even so, most schools the
model flags do not close in the next few years: closure is rare (about
`r pts(100 * TE$base, 1)` in 100 school-years), and many schools with the same
figures carry on, merge their classes, federate or find pupils.

## Simple warning signs {#sec-signs}

For governors and councils, five signs that can be read straight from a
school's own returns:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-signs
#| tbl-cap: "Five warning signs, how often closing schools showed them in the two years before closure, and how often other schools did."
sl <- c(small = "Small (under 100 pupils, primary; under 600, secondary)", falling = "Pupils down 15% or more over three years",
        deficit_in_year = "In-year deficit of more than 3% of income", reserve_neg = "Revenue reserve below zero",
        under_capacity = "Under 70% full")
dcast(F$sign_share, sign ~ stage, value.var = c("closing", "open"))[, .(Sign = sl[sign],
  `Primary, closing` = sprintf("%.0f%%", closing_Primary), `Primary, other` = sprintf("%.0f%%", open_Primary),
  `Secondary, closing` = sprintf("%.0f%%", closing_Secondary), `Secondary, other` = sprintf("%.0f%%", open_Secondary))] |>
  kt(align = "lrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-signs
#| fig-cap: "How many of the five signs a school showed in a year, and the share of such school-years followed by closure within two years, 2017-18 to 2023-24 (4 = four or five signs)."
#| fig-height: 3.6
ggplot(sr, aes(factor(n_signs), rate)) + geom_col(fill = DPURPLE, width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", rate)), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.4, colour = INK) +
  facet_wrap(~stage) + labs(x = "Warning signs", y = "% closing within two years") + theme_note(11) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15)))
```

A primary school with none of the signs closed within two years in
`r pts(sr_at("Primary", 0), 1)` cases in 100; with three,
`r pts(sr_at("Primary", 3), 1)`; with four or five,
`r pts(sr_at("Primary", 4), 1)`. The signs pick out a school that needs a
conversation about its future, not one that will close.

## Where the warning signs are now {#sec-now}

```{r}
#| include: false
BA <- F$by_area[, .(schools = sum(schools), flagged = sum(flagged), three_plus = sum(three_plus)), by = area][
  , `:=`(pct_flag = 100 * flagged / schools, pct_three = 100 * three_plus / schools)]
NOW <- F$now
```

Applied to each open school's latest return (`r paste(range(names(NOW$years)), collapse = " to ")`), the
model puts `r format(NOW$flagged, big.mark = ",")` of
`r format(NOW$schools, big.mark = ",")` schools
(`r pts(100 * NOW$flagged / NOW$schools, 1)`%) in the band that, over the
last seven years, held the riskiest 2% of school-years. That share is higher
than 2% because rolls are falling now in more places than they were. The map
counts them by authority.

```{r}
#| label: fig-now-map
#| fig-cap: "Open state schools whose latest return is in the highest-risk band (the riskiest 2% of school-years since 2017-18), as a share of the authority's schools with a return. No school is named."
b <- merge(DEM$bounds, BA, by = "area")
pal <- colorNumeric(c("#f7f7f7", "#e7d4e8", "#c2a5cf", "#9970ab", "#762a83"), c(0, max(15, ceiling(max(b$pct_flag, na.rm = TRUE)))))
leaflet(height = 560, options = leafletOptions(scrollWheelZoom = FALSE)) |>
  addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldGrayCanvas") |> setView(-1.6, 52.8, 6) |>
  addPolygons(data = b, fillColor = ~pal(pct_flag), fillOpacity = 0.85, color = "white", weight = 0.6,
              popup = ~sprintf("<b>%s</b><br>%d of %d schools in the highest-risk band (%.1f%%)<br>%d with three or more warning signs",
                               area, flagged, schools, pct_flag, three_plus)) |>
  addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = c(0, max(15, ceiling(max(b$pct_flag, na.rm = TRUE)))), title = "% of schools",
            labFormat = labelFormat(suffix = "%"), opacity = 0.9)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-now
DT::datatable(BA[order(-pct_flag), .(Area = area, Schools = schools, `Highest-risk band` = flagged, `%` = round(pct_flag, 1),
                                     `Three or more signs` = three_plus, `% ` = round(pct_three, 1))],
              rownames = FALSE, options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE),
              caption = "Open state mainstream schools with a recent return, by authority: how many are in the highest-risk band, and how many show three or more of the five warning signs. No school is named.")
```

## Sussex: the schools that closed {#sec-fin-sussex}

The closed schools can be named. Each of these Sussex primary schools'
last years:

```{r}
#| label: fig-sussex-closed
#| fig-cap: "Sussex primary schools that closed or merged from 2019/20: pupils as a share of capacity, and revenue reserve as a share of income, in the years before closure."
#| fig-height: 6.6
ex <- F$examples[stage == "Primary"][, lab := paste0(stringr::str_wrap(name, 30), "\n(", area, ", ", tolower(event), " ", yl(last_year), ")")]
exl <- melt(ex, id.vars = c("lab", "k"), measure.vars = c("util", "reserve_pct"))
exl[, variable := factor(variable, c("util", "reserve_pct"), c("Pupils as % of capacity", "Revenue reserve, % of income"))]
ggplot(exl[!is.na(value)], aes(k, value, colour = variable)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = LIGHT) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 1.4) + facet_wrap(~lab, ncol = 4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(DPURPLE, BPURPLE)) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(-6, -3, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Years before closure (0 = last year)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) + theme_note(9)
```

## What this cannot tell you {#sec-fin-limits}

- **Closure is a decision, not a measurement.** Councils, dioceses and
  trusts close schools for many reasons: falling rolls and money, but also
  buildings, standards, reorganisation (infant and junior schools merging)
  and local politics. The model describes the schools that were closed, not
  the ones that should have been.
- **The last year is partly the decision itself.** Once closure is proposed,
  parents move children and rolls fall faster, which is why the early test
  (two or three years ahead) matters more than the headline one.
- **Academies and maintained schools differ.** Academies rarely close: they
  are moved to another trust. In a multi-academy trust an academy's reserve
  is its own share, and the trust's central reserve can carry it.
- **The returns differ in timing and coverage.** CFR years run April to
  March, AAR years September to August; some schools miss a year; capacity is
  GIAS's latest figure, not the figure each year.
- **A warning is not a forecast for one school.** Most schools showing the
  signs do not close in the next few years. That is why no open school is
  named here.

## Data and calculations {#sec-fin-data}

**Finances.** DfE's [Financial Benchmarking and Insights
Tool](https://financial-benchmarking-and-insights-tool.education.gov.uk/data-sources)
files: CFR full data workbooks for local authority maintained schools,
financial years 2014-15 to 2025-26, and AAR downloads for academies,
2016-17 to 2024-25. From each return: pupils (full-time equivalent, including
dual registrations where given), total income, total expenditure (as DfE
defines them in each year), staff costs and the revenue reserve. The in-year
balance is income minus expenditure. Central services rows of multi-academy
trusts are left out. A CFR year (April to March) is labelled with the
academic year it mostly falls in.

**One school, several numbers.** A school's earlier URNs are joined to its
latest through GIAS's one-to-one predecessor links (academy conversion, a
change of type), not through mergers. Where a year has two returns (a
part-year CFR and an AAR around conversion), the one with the larger income
is kept.

**Measures.** Change in pupils over three years; pupils as a percentage of
capacity (GIAS's latest recorded capacity); revenue reserve and in-year
balance as percentages of income; income per pupil; staff costs as a
percentage of expenditure. Percentiles are among the state mainstream
schools of the same stage still open that year.

**Closures.** As on [Pupil numbers and school places](demographics.qmd#sec-demog-data):
state mainstream schools closed with no successor or merged, from GIAS, with
the last academic year taught. A return for year *t* counts as "closing within
two years" if the school's last year is *t*+1 or *t*+2; returns in or after the
last year are left out. The early test uses *t*+2 or *t*+3 and leaves out the
year before closure.

**Current schools.** Each open school's latest return (2023-24 or later), with
the model fitted on every year. The highest-risk band is the predicted risk
above which the riskiest 2% of school-years from 2017-18 to 2023-24 fall.
School-level scores are kept out of the published data.

The code is `R/43_finance_closures.R`, which writes `data/finance_closures.rds`.
